note: The ONE truth table for a catalogued `type: "bool"` automation knob, shared by both implementations of it: service/automations/_common.py::bool_knob and app/lib/boolKnob.ts::boolKnob. Two halves of one rule that cannot share code across the wire, so they share this table instead — add a row here and whichever half drifts goes red. Read by test_automation_rules_api.case_bool_knob_matches_the_typescript_half and app/lib/boolKnob.test.ts.
contract: A key that is present-but-null SAYS NOTHING, so it means what an absent key means: the declared default. Every other stored value is read with PYTHON truthiness, because the relay is the side that acts on it — an empty list or an empty object is OFF on both sides, not ON on one of them.

cases.name: explicit true beats a false default
explicit false beats a true default
the string "false" is ON — it is non-empty, and this is why a bool knob must never be typed by hand into raw JSON
